author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first then last). Specialties with no vet still appear; vets with no specialty do not. All specialties on one page, no pagination.
acceptance_criteria: Every stored specialty is listed by its stored name
Each specialty shows the veterinarians holding it, rendered first name then last name (e.g. Helen Leary)
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian beneath it
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on the page (the page indexes specialties, not the vet roster)
All specialties render on a single page with no pagination
The page is read-only: it adds, changes, and removes nothing (NG-2 unchanged)
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only server-rendered page in the vet feature package, built entirely from existing patterns. It reuses the feature-package + declarative-Spring-Data-repository + Thymeleaf-SSR shape and adds one thin element: a new SpecialtyRepository that mirrors owner/PetTypeRepository exactly (a lookup-value repo returning all rows in name order via a JPQL ORDER BY query). (1) Controller placement: extend the existing VetController with a showSpecialtyList handler rather than adding a thin second controller. The endpoint is another read-only page in the same bounded context; VetController already serves two vet routes, and the feature-package convention groups a feature's controllers together. Matches the prd-entry file_targets. (2) Projection: a vet-driven traversal cannot satisfy 'a specialty held by no vet must still appear' because orphan specialties are unreachable from any Vet, so the specialty list must come from its own table via the new SpecialtyRepository. The vet-to-specialty association is @ManyToMany(fetch=FetchType.EAGER) on Vet (Vet.java:47), so VetRepository.findAll() returns vets with specialties fully initialized: no LazyInitializationException despite open-in-view being disabled, and no surprise N+1 (eager join). Build the inverse map in the controller: seed one entry per specialty from SpecialtyRepository, then iterate the eagerly-fetched vets and file each under the specialties it holds. Vets with no specialty contribute nothing and are naturally excluded; orphan specialties survive because they seed the map. Reuse the @Cacheable VetRepository.findAll() as-is. (3) No ADR: no new pattern, module, integration, or trade-off. system-design.md Contracts updated (new SpecialtyRepository row; REQ-VET-003 wired into Specialty and VetController).
integration_points: GET /specialties.html on VetController returns view name vets/specialtyList (product owner named the route explicitly; honor it)
new SpecialtyRepository injected into VetController alongside the existing VetRepository

controller assembles an ordered view model (recommend a small record, e.g. an ordered list of {specialty name, ordered list of holding vets}) and adds it under one model attribute; prefer a typed record list over a Map so template iteration order is unambiguous

patterns.description: direct precedent for the new SpecialtyRepository: a lookup-value Spring Data repo whose read method returns every row ordered by name via an explicit @Query('... ORDER BY x.name'). Mirror it as SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() ORDER BY s.name. (Oracle N/A on this run — not in tool list; confirmed the pattern and the EAGER fetch by Read, not search_symbol.)

layout-fragment convention the new template must follow: th:replace="~{fragments/layout :: layout (~{::body},'vets')}" with the 'vets' menu active. The prd-entry's template path src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html is confirmed correct (feature-grouped under templates/vets/). vetList.html:18 also shows the exact 'firstName + " " + lastName' full-name rendering the acceptance criteria require.

risks.risk: Ordering left arbitrary would violate edge cases 1 and 3 (stable order of specialties and of vets under each).
risks.mitigation: Order specialties by stored name via the repository query's ORDER BY s.name (consistent with Vet.getSpecialties() and PetTypeRepository). Order the vets under each specialty by last name then first name — a stable, deterministic comparator — while still rendering them 'first last'.

risks.risk: Reaching for a vet-only traversal to derive the projection would silently drop specialties held by no vet.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate specialties from SpecialtyRepository as the outer set; use the vet collection only to populate holders.

notes: Verdict minor: one new declarative repository mirroring an existing one, one controller handler, one template — an established pattern applied once more, not new design ground. No ADR. Read-only page: adds/changes/removes nothing, so NG-2 is preserved. dispatch-start at line 3 recorded responding_to [1]; the active prd-entry is at line 2 (noted for provenance; records are append-only).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: XSS: specialtyList.html renders specialty name and vet names via th:text (auto-escaped); no th:utext or unescaped DOM sink introduced
Injection: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static parameterless JPQL @Query with no string concatenation; /specialties.html binds no request parameters
Data exposure: SpecialtyDirectoryEntry view model exposes only specialty name and formatted vet full-name strings; specialty ids used only as internal map keys, never rendered
DoS: unpaginated render is over an admin-curated reference table (accepted product trade-off, not attacker-controlled); no finding
Supply chain: no *.gradle or dependency changes; no new dependency added

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The guard `if (holders != null)` is dead code. `holdersBySpecialtyId` is seeded from `findSpecialties()`, which returns every row in the specialty table. A `Specialty` on a `Vet` from the FK-constrained `@ManyToMany` join table can only reference a row that exists in that table, so `holdersBySpecialtyId.get(specialty.getId())` cannot return null for any specialty `vet.getSpecialties()` yields. The guard silently swallows what would be a referential-integrity violation rather than surfacing it as a NullPointerException, hiding data corruption and adding noise without benefit.
findings.fix: Remove the null-guard and intermediate variable. Replace the three-line body `List<Vet> holders = holdersBySpecialtyId.get(specialty.getId()); if (holders != null) { holders.add(vet); }` with the single statement `holdersBySpecialtyId.get(specialty.getId()).add(vet);`.

findings.description: The final directory order is determined by re-iterating `specialties` (the list returned ordered by name from `findSpecialties()`), not by the map. `LinkedHashMap` is used only as a lookup structure keyed by specialty ID; its insertion-order guarantee is unused. Using `LinkedHashMap` over `HashMap` signals to the next reader that map iteration order matters for correctness — a false signal. Replace with `HashMap` to communicate that this is a lookup map, not an ordered structure.
findings.fix: Change `new LinkedHashMap<>()` to `new HashMap<>()` on the map initializer line, and replace the `import java.util.LinkedHashMap;` import with `import java.util.HashMap;`.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository faithfully: same JpaRepository extension, same @Query + ORDER BY pattern, same findXxx() naming convention (grep-confirmed; IDE not consulted)
Javadoc on buildSpecialtyDirectory clearly explains the seeding/filing logic and the orphan-specialty invariant
SpecialtyDirectoryEntry record is appropriately scoped as a controller-local view model; fields are typed (String, List<String>); no raw Object or Map
Comparator<Vet> by last name then first name is a correct and deterministic sort key, expressed cleanly
Stream pipeline in the directory-building step (sorted → map → toList) is idiomatic and readable
Template follows the layout-fragment convention from vetList.html: th:replace with vets menu active
No get/set prefixes on record accessors; record declared without mutable state

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test method names start with `specialtyDirectory...Should...` instead of `theSpecialtyDirectory...Should...`. The brief (§ Test Naming) mandates the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` school for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. The `the` prefix is missing from all five.

AC#3 is only half-covered. `specialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVet` asserts `containsString("surgery")` — surgery appears on the page — which is non-vacuous and would fail if the controller dropped holder-free specialties. However the second half of the criterion, "with no veterinarian beneath it", is never asserted. If a bug incorrectly attributed Helen Leary to surgery, all five tests would still pass. A complete test must also verify that the surgery entry carries no vet names, either via `model().attribute(...)` asserting the surgery SpecialtyDirectoryEntry has empty vetNames, or via a structural HTML check.

Specialty ordering is not asserted. The design-block requires specialties ordered by stored name (repository ORDER BY s.name); the controller preserves repository order. The two mock specialties `radiology` and `surgery` happen to be listed in alphabetical order in the `willReturn` stub, so reversing the rendered order cannot be detected by `containsString` checks. A test must return specialties in a non-alphabetical order from the mock and assert the rendered output restores alphabetical order, or assert rendered position (e.g. `radiology` appears before `surgery` in the response body).

Vet ordering under a specialty is not asserted. The design-block specifies vets under each specialty are sorted last-name-then-first-name before rendering. The current fixture has only one vet (Helen Leary) holding any specialty, so ordering is structurally unobservable. A test must add a second fixture vet holding the same specialty (with a name that sorts differently) and verify the rendered order.

AC#6 — "The page is read-only: it adds, changes, and removes nothing (NG-2 unchanged)" — has no dedicated test. The controller is `@GetMapping`-only and makes no write calls, giving structural read-only proof. Whether the PRD intends a behavioral assertion (e.g., verifying no write mock methods are invoked) or accepts the structural constraint of a GET-only handler as sufficient is a product decision.

approved_aspects: specialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVetWithNoSpecialty uses not(containsString("James Carter")) — non-vacuous because test 2 proves Helen Leary is rendered, confirming the vet-name rendering machinery is active and selective

specialtyDirectoryShouldShowHoldingVetsByFullName checks containsString("Helen Leary") against the rendered HTTP response body (not model state), and the exact substring "Helen Leary" would fail if the template emitted "Leary Helen"

specialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage uses hasSize(2) + attributeDoesNotExist("totalPages") — not tautological; hasSize(2) would fail if the controller dropped any specialty, attributeDoesNotExist would fail if pagination were added

@MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository accepted as tolerated continuity: the existing class already uses @MockitoBean VetRepository in a @WebMvcTest context; a JPA-repository hand-written double would require implementing ~30 JpaRepository methods; the brief tolerance clause explicitly covers this existing pattern
Factory methods radiology(), surgery(), james(), helen() properly encapsulate object construction per the brief; no bare mystery literals
All five tests pass cleanly against the real MVC dispatch and Thymeleaf rendering pipeline

findings.description: REQ-SYS-001 open item judgment: the specialty directory page uses the standard layout fragment (confirmed at specialtyList.html:3: th:replace with layout, vets active), which carries navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory. author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: veterinarians grouped by specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory listing every specialty by stored name, each with its holding veterinarians by full name on one unpaged page; specialties held by no vet still listed, vets holding none omitted.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name.
Given a specialty held by one or more veterinarians, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holding veterinarian is shown by full name with the first name before the last name.
Given a specialty that no veterinarian holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then that specialty is still listed with no veterinarian beneath it.
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian does not appear on the page.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them appear on a single page with no paging.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2): the specialty directory reads existing records only and neither adds, changes, nor removes anything; the read-only property is a scope boundary carried by NG-2, not a testable Done-when criterion — the GET-only handler is structural proof, so no dedicated no-write test is warranted.
notes: Processed two review findings. (1) doc-reviewer autofix at docs/prd.md:125 applied verbatim: the 38-word sentence was split into two sentences, no duplicate 'Helen Leary' parenthetical. (2) test-reviewer clarify on AC#6 (read-only): confirmed as owner that read-only is a scope restatement of NG-2, not an independently testable behavior; it stays as edge case 4 referencing NG-2, not a Done-when criterion; no PRD change needed for it. The five Done-when criteria map 1:1 onto the five existing tests.
